key_insight: Park and Walsh show that reinforcement learning can guide generative models to propose crystal structures that are not only novel and diverse, but also thermodynamically stable and useful for targeted properties. This turns crystal discovery from mostly random generation into a more directed search process.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of discovering new crystalline materials in the enormous search space of possible structures, where most generated candidates are either unstable, repetitive, or unlikely to meet desired property targets.
method: Use a reinforcement learning loop to steer a generative model toward crystal structures with higher reward scores.
Define rewards around thermodynamic stability, diversity, novelty, and desired material properties.
Iteratively improve candidate generation so the model explores promising regions of crystal design space more efficiently.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work is a strong example of combining generative modeling with reinforcement learning to control outputs under multiple constraints. It highlights a practical strategy for using AI to accelerate scientific discovery in high-dimensional design spaces.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing generative model -> RL reward -> improved crystal candidates

paper_title: Guiding generative models to uncover diverse and novel crystals via reinforcement learning
